name: MathlibAnnex.Sphere.nonempty_isometryEquiv_iff_nonempty_linearIsometryEquiv_of_finiteDimensional
title: The unit-sphere chord metric determines the ambient normed space

content.display_title: The unit-sphere chord metric determines the ambient normed space
content.one_sentence_role: Classifies existence of ambient linear isometries from the unit-sphere chord metric.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $X,Y$ be real normed vector spaces and assume
$$\dim_{\mathbb R}X<\infty\quad\text{or}\quad\dim_{\mathbb R}Y<\infty.$$
Let $S_X=\{x:\|x\|_X=1\}$ and $S_Y=\{y:\|y\|_Y=1\}$, with chord distances $d_X(u,v)=\|u-v\|_X$ and $d_Y(u,v)=\|u-v\|_Y$. A sphere isometry equivalence is a bijection $\Delta:S_X\to S_Y$ preserving these distances. A real linear isometry equivalence is a real linear bijection $A:X\to Y$ satisfying $\|Ax\|_Y=\|x\|_X$ for every $x$. Then
$$\bigl(\exists\text{ a sphere isometry equivalence }S_X\to S_Y\bigr)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\bigl(\exists\text{ a real linear isometry equivalence }X\to Y\bigr).$$
content.assumptions: The real normed-space structures and the finite-dimensional disjunction are the inputs. Neither positive dimension, completeness nor initial finite-dimensionality of both spaces is an extra assumption.
content.conclusion: The theorem equates existence statements. It does not assert that the recovered ambient map restricts to a specified $\Delta$. Zero-dimensional spaces and empty unit spheres are included.
content.proof_summary: Transfer finite dimension in either direction, separate zero dimension, transport the positive-dimensional case to norm models, recover a linear isometry there, and compose back. Conversely restrict an ambient linear isometry.

proof_steps.text:
**Transfer dimension in the applicable direction.** Given $\Delta$, if $X$ is finite-dimensional, [finite dimension transfer along a sphere isometry](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Sphere/Dimension.lean#L39-L47) makes $Y$ finite-dimensional. If $Y$ is finite-dimensional, apply it to $\Delta^{-1}$ to make $X$ finite-dimensional. Then [equality of dimensions](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Sphere/Dimension.lean#L79-L85) gives $\dim_{\mathbb R}X=\dim_{\mathbb R}Y=n$. If $n=0$, both spaces consist only of zero; the unique map $0\mapsto0$ is a real linear isometry equivalence. The sphere restriction is the empty bijection. [the finite-dimensional construction including zero](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Sphere/MetricRigidity.lean#L91-L120) separates this case before using positive-dimensional coordinates. The dimension-transfer input is made explicit by the radial map
$$R_\Delta(x)=
\begin{cases}0,&x=0,\\
\|x\|_X\Delta(x/\|x\|_X),&x\ne0.
\end{cases}$$
Its inverse is $R_{\Delta^{-1}}$. The radial estimates are $\|R_\Delta(x)-R_\Delta(y)\|_Y\le3\|x-y\|_X$ and the analogous inverse inequality. Both maps are continuous, and these Lipschitz bounds in both directions give equality of Hausdorff dimensions. A finite-dimensional $X$ is locally compact; its radial homeomorphism makes $Y$ locally compact, which forces finite-dimensionality for a real normed space. With both finite-dimensional, their Hausdorff dimensions equal their real dimensions. This use of the radial map proves dimension transfer; it does not identify the recovered linear $A$ with $R_\Delta$.

**Use one coordinate system on each space.** For $n=m+1>0$, choose continuous real linear equivalences $e_X:\mathbb R^n\to X$ and $e_Y:\mathbb R^n\to Y$. Define
$$p(x)=\|e_Xx\|_X,\qquad q(x)=\|e_Yx\|_Y.$$
The operator bounds for these equivalences and their inverses give positive comparisons with the reference sup norm. Transport the given sphere map by
$$\Delta_M=(e_Y|_{\{q=1\}})^{-1}\circ\Delta\circ(e_X|_{\{p=1\}}).$$
For $p(u)=p(v)=1$,
$$q(\Delta_Mu-\Delta_Mv)
=\|\Delta(e_Xu)-\Delta(e_Xv)\|_Y
=\|e_Xu-e_Xv\|_X=p(u-v).$$
These are [the coordinate norm models](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Module/EquivalentSeminorm/Transport.lean#L81-L111) and [exact sphere transport](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Module/EquivalentSeminorm/Transport.lean#L141-L163). More explicitly, for $e=e_X$ or $e_Y$ its model record has
$$p_e(x)=\|ex\|,\qquad
a_e=(\max(\|e^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}},1))^{-1},\qquad
b_e=\max(\|e\|_{\mathrm{op}},1).$$
Both constants are positive. The inverse bound
$\|x\|_\infty\le\|e^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|ex\|$
gives $a_e\|x\|_\infty\le p_e(x)$; the direct bound gives
$p_e(x)\le b_e\|x\|_\infty$; continuity is the composition of $e$ with the norm. These specify the seminorm, two constants, positivity, lower and upper comparisons and continuity fields. The model carrier is the same vector space with norm $p_e$; the reference and model conversions are identity on values, zero and subtraction. On the sphere $p_e(u)=1$, so $u\mapsto eu$ and $y\mapsto e^{-1}y$ give the two inverse subtype maps used in $\Delta_M$.

**Recover in the models and compose back.** With standard Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^n$, put $K_p=\{p\le1\}$, $v_p=\lambda(K_p)$, and
$$\mathcal P_p^N=\operatorname{conv}_{\mathbb R}\{\pm v_p\Pi_n(B):
\ B:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^N,\ \forall x,\|Bx\|_\infty\le p(x)\},$$
where $B$ ranges over real linear maps and $\Pi_n(B)$ is the increasing-row maximal-minor vector. Define $\mathcal P_q^N$ similarly. The sphere isometry $\Delta_M$ gives equality of these bodies for every $N$, by [sphere-induced body invariance](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/BodyInvariance.lean#L188-L194). Input these models and all body equalities to [norm-preserving linear recovery](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/ModelRigidity.lean#L39-L47), as in [sphere-metric recovery in norm models](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/ModelRigidity.lean#L49-L56), obtaining bijective real linear $L$ with $q(Lx)=p(x)$. The same maps give
$$A=e_Y\circ L\circ e_X^{-1},\qquad
\|Ax\|_Y=q(L(e_X^{-1}x))=p(e_X^{-1}x)=\|x\|_X.$$
The inverse is $e_X\circ L^{-1}\circ e_Y^{-1}$. This is [coordinate model recovery and return](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Sphere/ModelTransport.lean#L11-L23). It proves existence, without claiming $A|_{S_X}=\Delta$.

**Restrict an ambient linear isometry for the converse.** Given $A$, the equations $\|Au\|_Y=\|u\|_X=1$ and the corresponding inverse equation make its restriction a sphere bijection. For $u,v\in S_X$,
$$d_Y(Au,Av)=\|A(u-v)\|_Y=\|u-v\|_X=d_X(u,v).$$
Thus the restriction is a sphere isometry equivalence, including the empty case, as in [restriction of a linear isometry](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Sphere/MetricRigidity.lean#L56-L90).

content.lean_realization_notes: The conclusion is an equivalence of existence statements, not an extension assertion for the supplied $\Delta$. When both spaces are initially known to be finite-dimensional, the [two-sided finite-dimensional version](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Sphere/MetricRigidity.lean#L134-L145) gives the same equivalence. The [finite-dimensional-domain implication](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Sphere/MetricRigidity.lean#L146-L153) and [finite-dimensional-codomain implication](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Sphere/MetricRigidity.lean#L155-L163) use the respective side of the present disjunction; the [combined forward implication](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Sphere/MetricRigidity.lean#L165-L176) selects the applicable direction. These variants preserve the same existence conclusion and do not supply an agreement condition with $\Delta$.
